skill.name: routeros-netinstall
skill.description: Guides RouterOS Netinstall planning for MikroTik devices, including netinstall-cli flags, package naming, first-boot scripts, etherboot setup, and host networking requirements.
skill.summary: Plan MikroTik RouterOS Netinstall commands, packages, scripts, and recovery workflows.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting and examples. Confirmed risks are the sudo Netinstall commands, privileged interface configuration, a security-relevant vendor download, and a private IP setup example. Semantic review found no prompt injection, but it found root execution after download, destructive flashing risk, and first-boot device-mode changes.

remediation.issue: Privileged Netinstall commands can reflash devices or alter host networking.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sudo commands, and document target device, interface, backup, and maintenance checks.

remediation.issue: The quick-start downloads a binary and later runs it with sudo.
remediation.suggestion: Add checksum or signature verification steps before extraction and privileged execution.

remediation.issue: Mode scripts can change device mode and enable containers during first boot.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to review every mode script and explain the security effects before using the mode script flag.

remediation.issue: The static IP example can disrupt the wrong host interface.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to replace interface and address values only after confirming an isolated Netinstall segment.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The destructive reformat behavior is explicitly documented, and the later example provides a reinstall command. This is legitimate Netinstall behavior but a real availability and data-loss risk.

content.value_statement: RouterOS recovery and reinstall workflows are easy to misorder. This skill gives grounded Netinstall guidance for packages, scripts, interfaces, and first boot behavior.
actual_capabilities: Explains official netinstall-cli syntax and option meanings.
Distinguishes configure scripts from one-time mode scripts.
Lists RouterOS package URL patterns and architecture naming rules.
Shows command patterns for reinstall, empty config, and preserved configuration.
Highlights etherboot, BOOTP, TFTP, and host networking requirements.
limitations: It does not verify package checksums or signatures.
It cannot detect router architecture without user supplied context.
It does not replace MikroTik release notes or support guidance.
It describes privileged commands that require careful human approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a router reinstall
use_cases.description: Prepare a RouterOS Netinstall workflow with package order, interface setup, and configuration behavior.

use_cases.title: Document recovery procedures
use_cases.description: Create repeatable recovery notes for teams that restore MikroTik routers after failed upgrades.

use_cases.title: Build Netinstall tooling
use_cases.description: Use grounded command examples and package rules when writing wrappers around netinstall-cli.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Netinstall Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation before using RouterOS Netinstall.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what RouterOS netinstall-cli does, when to use it, and what data it may erase. Keep the answer concise.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Package Names
prompt_templates.scenario: Map a RouterOS version and architecture to package names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given RouterOS version <version> and architecture <arch>, list the expected system package and all_packages file names.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Install Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a specific command while checking risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a netinstall-cli command for interface <interface>, architecture <arch>, and RouterOS version <version>. Include risks and approval checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design First-Boot Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for configure scripts and mode scripts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this RouterOS first-boot goal and propose whether to use -s or -sm. Explain script order, persistence, and security impact.

output_examples.input: I need to reinstall an ARM64 router and keep its configuration.
output: Confirm the device is backed up and in etherboot mode.
Use the ARM64 system package first in the package list.
Avoid the empty configuration flag when preserving the configuration database.
Remember that local files and application databases may not be preserved.

output_examples.input: I want a first-boot script to enable container mode.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a mode script because it runs before default configuration. It would warn that device mode changes can reboot the router and change security posture.

output_examples.input: What package file should I use for x86 RouterOS 7.22?
output_examples.output: The skill would explain that x86 is the exception. The system package omits the architecture suffix, while the all-packages archive still includes x86.

best_practices: Confirm the target device, interface, packages, and backup status before running Netinstall.
Use a dedicated isolated Layer 2 segment with no competing DHCP server.
Verify downloaded packages and binaries before using sudo or flashing devices.
anti_patterns: Running examples on a production interface without confirming the target MAC address.
Using the force flag to ignore storage checks without validating package size and device model.
Treating a configure script as temporary when it persists across reset-configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill run Netinstall automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any command execution still requires tool access and human approval.

faq.question: Why does Netinstall require sudo?
faq.answer: Netinstall uses privileged BOOTP, DHCP, and TFTP behavior on a local interface. Linux normally requires root privileges for that work.

faq.question: Will Netinstall erase my router?
faq.answer: Yes, it reformats the RouterOS system drive. Some modes preserve the configuration database, but files and application databases may be lost.

faq.question: Can it help choose package names?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents RouterOS architecture suffixes and the x86 naming exception.

faq.question: What is the difference between configure scripts and mode scripts?
faq.answer: Configure scripts persist as custom default configuration. Mode scripts run once during the first boot after Netinstall.

faq.question: Should I use this on a production network?
faq.answer: Use it only with a planned maintenance window, backups, and an isolated Layer 2 segment.
